summary: Component catalog is the generated inventory of exported Hoplight UI entries. scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts scans React components throughout src/ui plus exported create/build/swatch/inject helpers under src/ui/_shared. Authors do not hand-edit the markdown: regenerate it with bun run scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts, and the pre-commit --check gate fails when live exports drift. Each row records Name, source File, TypeScript Signature, optional Doc blurb, and Styles class list. Before building a control, scan this catalog and reuse an existing entry rather than inventing a twin. The two tables distinguish React `.tsx` components from shared `.ts` UI helpers; that distinction is file shape and API role, not a claim that helpers are legacy or awaiting migration. Use the catalog as lookup authority for props and file homes; behavior and layout truth remain in reference/ui and the owning source.

sections.title: Components (React, `.tsx`)
sections.summary: Primary table of React .tsx exports that power the studio under ADR-008. Rows span shell chrome, shared components under src/ui/components, app-scoped presenters, and every Settings section including ConnectionsSection for MCP configuration. Workbench includes revision-aware character, lorebook, pack, persona, preset, regex, and quick-reply editors plus their rails, panes, health surfaces, LivePreview, and the LinkedSets control that attaches regex and quick-reply pieces to presets. Library contributes creation, import, and damaged-file controls; settings contributes model, connection, remote, and update controls; docs contributes its room and navigation. Each generated row records Name, source File, TypeScript Signature, optional Doc one-liner, and Styles class tokens. Prefer matching an existing name and path over adding a parallel control; empty Doc cells still identify reusable exports.

sections.title: Shared UI helpers (`src/ui/_shared`, `.ts`)
sections.summary: Secondary table for exported TypeScript UI helpers under src/ui/_shared whose names begin create, build, swatch, or inject. These are ordinary `.ts` functions rather than JSX components; the table makes no deprecation or migration claim. It uses the same Name, File, Signature, Doc, and Styles columns as the React table. The current entry is buildTimeline from version-history, a pure helper actively consumed by the React Updates surface to derive release relations and behind counts. Regenerating the catalog adds or removes rows as matching exports change. Open this table when a UI task needs shared computation or construction logic, and open the React table when it needs a rendered control.
